title: Episode 71 — The Conclusion of the Return-Guest Trilogy, with Bobby Lee
summary: The episode opens in an unfinished new studio, then devotes most of its running time to an on-air reconstruction of a nineteen-year-old fan's first sexual encounter with the host. The guest participates and sometimes gives specific affirmative answers, but the record also contains disputed proxy narration, an eighteen-year age gap, celebrity and group power, thigh-blocking, pain, nervous laughter, decision deference, repeated requests, and disclosure of her location, school, family, body, images, and sexual history. The archive preserves the contradictions without republishing that dossier. Bobby Lee then recounts childhood sexual abuse, a commercial-sex encounter with a possibly underage worker who was crying and shaking, and a later machete robbery he interprets as moral punishment and the catalyst for beginning stand-up. The cast gives contradictory ages for the worker; adult status is unresolved. Continued intercourse after visible distress is marked as an attributed consent failure, not normalized as comedy. Later remorse is retained but does not erase the described harm. Current consent, condom, STI, contraception, anatomy, trauma, disability, orientation, and trafficking guidance accompanies the record.
sensitivity: Explicit sexual content; young-adult fan and celebrity power imbalance; disputed consent and nonverbal stopping signals; private intimate images and identity triangulation; pregnancy, contraception and STI misinformation; bleeding and anatomy misinformation; childhood sexual abuse; disability slurs; possible minor in commercial sex; visible sex-worker distress; attributed sexual violence; trafficking risk; robbery and death threat; drugs and smuggling; racial, ethnic, gender-identity and disability slurs; trauma minimization; private former partners and medical details.
speaker_policy: Named dialogue remains withheld. Episode 71 has zero diarized turns and five coarse window embeddings for a large ensemble. Public guests and cast are contextually known, but no independently held-out multispeaker validation has passed.

source_notes.claim: Consent must be clear, voluntary, ongoing and specific; pulling away, freezing, silence, hesitation and other nonverbal signals require stopping and checking in

source_notes.claim: Arousal, lubrication and orgasm are involuntary bodily responses and do not equal consent

source_notes.claim: Withdrawal does not protect against STIs; consistent correct condom use reduces STI risk
source_notes.use: corrects tantric ejaculation and pull-out claims

source_notes.claim: Testing and sharing results reduce uncertainty, but condoms remain a core prevention strategy and many infections can be asymptomatic

source_notes.claim: Pain or bleeding can happen with first vaginal intercourse but do not happen to everyone; the hymen and bleeding do not prove virginity

source_notes.claim: Commercial sex induced by force, fraud or coercion is trafficking; any commercial sex involving a person under eighteen is trafficking regardless of force
source_notes.use: frames the contradictory age account, raid, crying, shaking and payment without making an unsupported legal finding

source_notes.claim: Sexual assault is sexual contact without clear, voluntary and informed consent
source_notes.use: frames attributed intercourse after visible distress while avoiding adjudication from a transcript

source_notes.claim: Consent applies independently to intimate-image sharing and online publication
source_notes.use: supports withholding young-guest and former-partner images

source_notes.claim: Exploitation of a minor in commercial sex is trafficking and online tools can facilitate that exploitation
